messages:
sam l: FYI customer 'AcmePayments' flagged their AWS Marketplace invoice vs our dashboard. AWS line items show ~3,200 "units" on 2026-02-18 invoice but our token ledger shows ~1,050,000 tokens which doesn't map cleanly. Invoice ID: AWS-INV-30921. Anyone seen this unit->token conversion issue?
priya r: Do we know the product code / sku? sometimes marketplace publishes quantity in 'usage hours' or '10k token blocks'.
jordan k: Product code is 'redwood-inference:prod-rl-01' per the invoice, SKU: rl-prod-v1. I asked the customer for the CSV export.
elena f: @matt (finance) can you pull the marketplace report for that invoice period (Feb 15-20)? curious if AWS aggregated multiple accounts under the same line item. :thinking:
matt (finance): Pulling now. Quick note: AWS sometimes bills by units where 1 unit = 1,000 compute-requests in their reporting schema. Could be a unit-of-measure mismatch. I'll attach raw lineitems in a sec.
sam l: Customer claims their portal shows 1.05M tokens for that account id (acct-9876). They expected ~ $1,100 but AWS charged $3,200. They want an explanation before filing a dispute. We need a root cause or repro.
priya r: Jordan, can you run our internal usage export for acct-9876 between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28? I want to compare our ledger to the customer's CSV. Quick SQL I use:```sql
SELECT day, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage_ledger
WHERE account_id = 'acct-9876' AND day BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```
jordan k: Ran the export. Total tokens = 1,049,720 for Feb. I'll attach the CSV to the thread.
priya r: Thanks. Next step: match AWS line items. @matt (finance) can you paste the raw marketplace line item rows (quantity, unit, unitPrice, productCode)?
matt (finance): Paste of relevant AWS lines (sanitized):```
productCode: redwood-inference:prod-rl-01 | quantity: 3200 | unit: "Unit" | unitPrice: $1.00 | total: $3200
productCode: redwood-inference:prod-rl-01 | quantity: 50 | unit: "GB-Hours" | unitPrice: $0.10 | total: $5
```
priya r: Hmm. If AWS is reporting quantity=3200 Units and charges $1/unit, what does 1 Unit represent? Our pricing model maps tokens -> cents per 1k tokens. If 1 Unit==1k tokens, 3,200 units => 3.2M tokens, which would be higher than our ledger. If 1 Unit==1k requests or vCPU-hours it's different.
elena f: I recall Marketplace metering for SaaS can report "metering dimensions" with custom unit labels. Sometimes our metering client submitted units as "1" per request, vs our internal counting which aggregates tokens. Could be double-counting when a single request produces multiple metering calls (e.g., streaming chunks).
sam l: Customer said they did 8,200 API calls in period. If meter was called for each chunk (streaming), and each streaming response sent 3 chunks on average, that could inflate AWS quantity ~3x. Does our metering client emit per-chunk calls?
jordan k: Checking metering service logs for acct-9876: found repeated POSTs to AWS Metering API with payloads like {dimension: 'tokens', quantity: 1} for each chunk. Here's a sample log line: ```INFO 2026-02-18T14:12:07Z metering-client: acct=acct-9876 product=rl-prod-v1 quantity=1 stream_chunk=true request_id=req-42ab```
priya r: That looks like the bug. The client should batch chunk counts into a single metering event per request and send token counts, not per-chunk unit increments. So AWS would record 3x quantity if streaming produced 3 chunks.
matt (finance): That would reconcile: 8,200 requests * avg 3 chunks = 24,600 units, but invoice shows 3,200 units. Wait numbers don't match exactly. Could be multiple factors: chunking + rounding + previous month's carry-forward. Need exact mapping.
elena f: Also confirm whether our marketplace metering reports 'unit'=1 token or 'unit'=1 chunk. The metering client config file (metering.yaml) has a field 'unit_scale' that was recently changed in Jan. I suspect a regression.
sam l: Action items: 1) @jordan k gather metering logs for 2026-02-01..28 for acct-9876 and include request_id samples. 2) @elena f check metering client version rollouts around Jan 2026 and unit_scale default. 3) @matt (finance) open a support case with AWS Marketplace (I've got their case number if needed) and hold dispute until we confirm.
priya r: For immediate customer response: explain we're investigating and that AWS invoices reflect marketplace metering events we reported. Offer provisional credit if evidence shows client bug inflated counts.
sam l: I'm filing internal incident ticket: INC-2026-584 (metering-client unit-scale bug). Tagging @billing-bot to track refunds. :white_check_mark: 
matt (finance): Opened AWS support case: AWS-CASE-99312. I also asked for raw CSV from AWS to show any aggregated adjustments.
jordan k: Uploaded metering logs to /internal/billing/2026/acct-9876/metering-logs.zip and included sample request_ids. Attaching pointers to logs: request req-42ab, req-5f00, req-a933.
elena f: Found config change: metering.yaml v2.4.1 (deployed 2026-01-28) changed default unit_scale from 1000->1 to support finer-grain metering. That would invert mapping and cause AWS to see ~1000x difference for some customers unless the ingestion pipeline multiplies back. We'll need a migration patch.
sam l: Thanks team. Priya, can you draft a short customer message summarizing the current findings and expected timeline? I'll coordinate refunds if confirmed.
priya r: Draft to customer: "Thanks — we're investigating. Initial findings show our marketplace metering client changed unit scaling in late Jan which may have caused per-chunk counts to be sent as individual units. We're collecting logs and will update within 48 hours with either a correction or credit. Apologies for the confusion." Send if that looks good.
matt (finance): I'll pause dispute until we confirm with AWS raw CSV. If confirmed, we'll issue a one-off credit and adjust downstream accounting.
sam l: Good. Closing loop: mark this thread "investigating". Will follow up with root cause write-up after patch and customer resolution. :thumbsup:
